# CC14: 玉玲珑馆 Yulinglong Guan

Wave 3 · Changchun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=CC14` · Page: `/scenes/#CC14` · Row: `research/buildings/CC14-yulinglong-guan/`

## What it was

玉玲珑馆 Yulinglong Guan, "Hall of Exquisite Jade", stood on an island south of 狮子林 (S05 j83:17a; E0288). 日下旧闻考 gives the main range 正谊明道 of five bays, 林光澹碧 to the north (inner plaque 逰心於淡), 鹤安斋 to the east and 蹈和堂 to the south-west (E0288). Built 1747 and added to about 1764 (E0291). S361 describes a five-bay gate, the main hall 正谊明道 (it says seven bays against five in S05), a nine-bay rear hall 林光澹碧, a west court with 撷景室, 蹈和堂 and the square 朝晖亭 on the water, and an east court with the five-bay 鹤安斋, the double-eaved 狎鸥亭, 随安室, a greenhouse, a fountain, 澹然书屋 and 芥舟 on the shore (E0291). Cranes were kept and released at 鹤安斋 (E0289); the poems speak of Taihu rocks, bamboo and summer visits by boat (E0267, E0290). The name lasts in poems to 1807 (E0290). Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **built** by 1755 poem [j83:17b]; 1747; added to c. 1764; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S48, S01, S361).
